intent.raw_query: Bali for solo traveler, $1500 budget, beaches and yoga, July 2026 from LA

experiences.name: Sunrise Yoga at Campuhan Ridge Walk
experiences.description: Join an outdoor sunrise yoga session along the scenic Campuhan Ridge Walk in Ubud, surrounded by lush jungle and rice paddies. Many local instructors offer small group sessions here, combining gentle movement with breathtaking natural scenery. A deeply restorative experience perfect for yogis of all levels.

experiences.name: Seminyak Beach Sunset & Surf Lesson
experiences.description: Take a beginner-to-intermediate surf lesson on the golden sands of Seminyak Beach, one of Bali's most beautiful and accessible surf spots. After your lesson, relax on the beach and watch the legendary Bali sunset paint the sky in vivid oranges and pinks. Board rental and instructor are typically included.

experiences.name: Full-Day Yoga Retreat at The Yoga Barn
experiences.description: Spend a full day immersed in wellness at The Yoga Barn, one of Bali's most renowned holistic retreat centers. Attend multiple yoga classes ranging from Hatha to Vinyasa, enjoy a healthy organic lunch at the on-site café, and optionally add a sound healing or meditation session. A transformative experience in the heart of Ubud.

experiences.name: Nusa Dua Crystal-Clear Beach Snorkeling
experiences.description: Explore the calm, turquoise waters of Nusa Dua, Bali's most pristine beach enclave. Join a guided snorkeling tour to discover vibrant coral reefs and tropical fish just offshore. The protected bay offers ideal conditions for snorkeling, making it perfect for all experience levels. Equipment and a local guide are included.

experiences.name: Balinese Cooking Class & Organic Farm Visit
experiences.description: Visit a traditional organic farm in the Ubud countryside to hand-pick fresh ingredients, then learn to prepare authentic Balinese dishes such as satay lilit, lawar, and black rice pudding under the guidance of a local chef. This immersive cultural and culinary experience ends with a communal feast of everything you've cooked together.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Bali
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - arrival day
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - arrival day
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Ngurah Rai International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear immigration and customs, collect baggage, and arrange a pre-booked airport transfer or grab a Bluebird taxi to Aegean Bliss Resort, Bali. Check in, freshen up, and get settled into your beachfront accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable - in-flight or pre-arrival
meals.lunch: Not applicable - in-flight or pre-arrival
meals.dinner: Grab a late-night snack from a 24-hour warung (local eatery) near the resort or order from the hotel if available. Budget: ~IDR 30,000–60,000 (approx. $2–4 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Arrival is late at night. Keep Day 1 light — just check in and rest. Pre-book your airport transfer in advance to avoid overpriced touts. Confirm hotel check-in details ahead of time since arrival is after 10 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After waking, take a leisurely stroll along the beachfront outside Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy the warm Bali morning air (avg. 25°C) and get your bearings. Explore the immediate beach area and watch local fishermen start their day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearest beach (within walking distance of the resort) for your first full Bali beach experience. Rent a sun lounger for ~IDR 50,000, swim in the warm Indian Ocean, and soak up the atmosphere. Visit a local surf shop to inquire about beginner surf lessons for later in the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the beachfront strip to explore local warungs and shops. Watch the famous Bali sunset from the beach. Find a budget beachside warung for dinner and enjoy the relaxed evening vibe.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel if included, or visit a nearby local café for nasi goreng (fried rice) or bubur ayam (rice porridge). Budget: ~IDR 25,000–50,000 ($1.50–3 USD)
meals.lunch: Fresh coconut and fruit salad from a beach vendor, or a simple meal at a local warung. Budget: ~IDR 30,000–60,000 ($2–4 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a beachfront warung — try mie goreng (fried noodles) or grilled fish with rice. Budget: ~IDR 50,000–80,000 ($3–5 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Take it easy today — your body is still adjusting to the time zone. Stay hydrated and use sunscreen (UV index is high). The warm summer weather (25°C avg. high) is perfect for beach relaxation.

day_by_day.morning: Join a sunrise beach yoga session. Many budget-friendly yoga instructors and local studios in Bali offer outdoor beach yoga classes starting at 6:30–7:00 AM for around IDR 80,000–150,000 ($5–10 USD). Breathe in the ocean air while practicing sun salutations with the sound of waves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local area on a rented scooter (IDR 60,000–80,000/day). Visit a nearby temple such as Tanah Lot or Uluwatu (depending on resort location) to experience Balinese Hindu culture. Dress respectfully — sarongs are available to rent at temple entrances for ~IDR 15,000.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the beachfront for the sunset. Attend a free or low-cost Kecak fire dance performance if near Uluwatu (tickets ~IDR 100,000 / ~$6 USD). Dinner at a local spot afterward.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-yoga snack — banana and water, or a smoothie bowl from a local café. Budget: ~IDR 30,000–50,000 ($2–3 USD)
meals.lunch: Stop at a local warung during your scooter exploration — try babi guling (suckling pig) or a vegetarian gado-gado. Budget: ~IDR 40,000–70,000 ($2.50–4.50 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner near the evening activity venue or back near the resort. Grilled corn, satay skewers, and rice at a night market. Budget: ~IDR 50,000–80,000 ($3–5 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Scooter rental is the most budget-friendly way to get around Bali. Always wear a helmet and carry your international driving permit. Be cautious on narrow roads. Bring a light rain jacket as July can have occasional brief showers (30mm avg. rainfall).

day_by_day.morning: Morning yoga practice — either return to the beach yoga class or find a budget studio inland. Many Ubud-style yoga studios have satellite classes or drop-in sessions for IDR 100,000–150,000 ($6–10 USD). Focus on a restorative or vinyasa flow class to start the day mindfully.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local beach known for snorkeling or crystal-clear water (Blue Lagoon or Padang Bai area if accessible). Rent snorkel gear for ~IDR 50,000 and explore the vibrant underwater life. Alternatively, enjoy a long beach walk and collect shells.
day_by_day.evening: Head to a local night market (pasar malam) for an authentic budget dinner experience. Browse stalls selling satay, martabak (stuffed pancakes), fresh juices, and traditional Balinese sweets. Great for people-watching and immersing in local culture.

meals.breakfast: Acai bowl or banana pancakes at a budget café near the resort. Budget: ~IDR 35,000–60,000 ($2–4 USD)
meals.lunch: Beachside warung lunch — fresh grilled fish with sambal, rice, and vegetables. Budget: ~IDR 50,000–75,000 ($3–5 USD)
meals.dinner: Night market feast — mix of small dishes from multiple stalls. Budget: ~IDR 50,000–80,000 ($3–5 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Check tide times before snorkeling — best visibility is typically mid-morning. Bring reef-safe sunscreen to protect the coral ecosystem. Night markets usually start around 5–6 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Ubud — Bali's cultural heart. Hire a driver for the day (~IDR 300,000–400,000 / $18–25 USD split if traveling with others, or use a Grab/Gojek ride). Start with the Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary (entry ~IDR 80,000 / $5 USD) — walk among hundreds of macaque monkeys in a lush jungle temple setting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ubud Market for budget souvenirs, handmade goods, and local crafts. Practice your bargaining skills! Visit the Ubud Palace (Puri Saren) — free to view from outside. Walk along Jalan Hanoman to browse yoga studios, health cafés, and artisan shops.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Balinese dance performance in Ubud — tickets are ~IDR 100,000–150,000 ($6–10 USD). Return to the resort by private driver or arrange a Grab ride back. Relax at the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel or a quick local café before departing for Ubud. Budget: ~IDR 30,000–50,000 ($2–3 USD)
meals.lunch: Ubud's famous Warung Ibu Oka for babi guling or a vegetarian warung on Jalan Dewi Sita. Budget: ~IDR 50,000–80,000 ($3–5 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Ubud before the dance show, or grab a quick bite from a street stall. Budget: ~IDR 50,000–80,000 ($3–5 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Ubud is approximately 1–1.5 hours from the southern beach areas. Start early to maximize your time. Wear comfortable walking shoes as Ubud involves a lot of walking on uneven terrain. Ubud is slightly cooler and greener than the coast.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning. Sleep in, practice personal yoga or meditation on your hotel balcony or the beach. Journal, read, or simply enjoy the beachfront view. This is a deliberate slow day to recharge mid-trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local surf school for a beginner surf lesson (IDR 200,000–300,000 / $12–18 USD including board and instructor for 2 hours). Bali's warm waters and consistent waves make it ideal for first-timers. Beaches like Kuta, Legian, or Seminyak are great for learning.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a traditional Balinese massage at a local spa — budget options start at IDR 80,000–120,000 ($5–7 USD) for a 60-minute session. Afterward, enjoy a quiet dinner near the resort.

meals.breakfast: Smoothie bowl or tropical fruit platter from a beach café. Budget: ~IDR 35,000–55,000 ($2–3.50 USD)
meals.lunch: Light beach snack — fresh coconut, corn on the cob, or a sandwich from a local café. Budget: ~IDR 30,000–50,000 ($2–3 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a budget warung near the resort — try ayam bakar (grilled chicken) with plecing kangkung (water spinach in chili). Budget: ~IDR 50,000–75,000 ($3–5 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Surf lessons are widely available and very affordable in Bali. Book directly with beach instructors to get the best price. Avoid middlemen or hotel booking desks which add markups. Massages are a great budget luxury — always tip your therapist IDR 20,000–30,000.

day_by_day.morning: Take a sunrise hike or join a guided walk to a scenic viewpoint or rice terrace near the resort area. If near Ubud region, the Tegalalang Rice Terraces are iconic (small entrance donation ~IDR 15,000). Alternatively, explore a local waterfall such as Gitgit or Sekumpul (entry ~IDR 20,000–30,000).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the beach for a relaxed afternoon. Try stand-up paddleboarding (SUP) rental for ~IDR 100,000/hour. Alternatively, explore a new beach section you haven't visited yet. Collect memories, take photos, and enjoy the warm 25°C weather.
day_by_day.evening: Cook a simple meal or join a budget cooking class. Some local families offer affordable Balinese cooking experiences for IDR 200,000–300,000 ($12–18 USD) including market visit, cooking, and eating your creation.

meals.breakfast: Pre-hike energy breakfast — nasi goreng telur (fried rice with egg) at a local warung. Budget: ~IDR 25,000–40,000 ($1.50–2.50 USD)
meals.lunch: Packed snacks from a local minimart (Indomaret/Alfamart) for the hike, or eat at a warung near the rice terraces. Budget: ~IDR 30,000–50,000 ($2–3 USD)
meals.dinner: Enjoy the meal you cooked in the cooking class, or dine at a nearby warung. Budget: ~IDR 0–60,000 ($0–4 USD)

day_by_day.notes: The midpoint of your trip — a great time to reflect and adjust plans. Weather is warm and sunny with minimal rain expected. Stay hydrated during morning hikes. The cooking class is a wonderful cultural experience and doubles as dinner!

day_by_day.morning: Morning beach yoga session — either join a class or practice independently on the sand using a travel mat. Focus on a longer, more meditative practice today (60–90 minutes). The beach at sunrise is magical and the weather is ideal for outdoor yoga.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a different beach or coastal area by scooter. Visit hidden gem beaches that are less touristy — ask locals for recommendations. Bring snacks, water, and your camera. Spend time swimming, relaxing, and exploring tide pools.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a local temple ceremony if one is happening nearby — Balinese ceremonies are frequent and visitors are often welcome to observe respectfully (dress modestly, wear a sarong). Check with your hotel about upcoming ceremonies.

meals.breakfast: Fruit smoothie and toast at a beachside café. Budget: ~IDR 30,000–50,000 ($2–3 USD)
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch at the hidden beach — buy supplies from a local market (fresh fruit, snacks, water). Budget: ~IDR 30,000–50,000 ($2–3 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local warung back near the resort. Try lawar (traditional Balinese mixed dish) or bebek betutu (slow-cooked duck). Budget: ~IDR 50,000–80,000 ($3–5 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Ask your hotel staff about upcoming local temple festivals or odalan (temple anniversary ceremonies). These are free to observe and offer an incredible window into Balinese Hindu culture. Always dress respectfully and follow local customs.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nusa Penida or Nusa Lembongan (if accessible from your resort location). Take a fast boat from Sanur Beach (~IDR 150,000–200,000 one way / $9–12 USD). Nusa Penida is famous for stunning cliffs, crystal-clear water, and Instagram-worthy viewpoints like Kelingking Beach and Angel's Billabong.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the island by rented scooter (~IDR 80,000/day on the island). Visit Broken Beach and Angel's Billabong for dramatic coastal scenery. Swim at Crystal Bay — one of Bali's clearest beaches. The water is warm and visibility for snorkeling is excellent.
day_by_day.evening: Return by fast boat to Sanur before sunset (last boats typically depart around 4–5 PM). Travel back to the resort and enjoy a relaxing evening. Treat yourself to a cold Bintang beer at a beachfront bar (~IDR 35,000).

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before departure — keep it light. Local café nasi goreng or fruit. Budget: ~IDR 25,000–40,000 ($1.50–2.50 USD)
meals.lunch: Lunch on Nusa Penida at a local warung near the beach — fresh seafood or simple Indonesian dishes. Budget: ~IDR 50,000–80,000 ($3–5 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner near Sanur or back at the resort area. Grilled seafood platter at a budget spot. Budget: ~IDR 60,000–100,000 ($4–6 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Book your fast boat in advance, especially in July (peak season). Nusa Penida roads are rough — drive carefully on the scooter. Bring motion sickness tablets if needed for the boat crossing. Wear water shoes for rocky beaches. This is a full day — start early!

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning at the beach. Practice yoga or meditation on the sand independently. Journal about your trip experiences so far. Visit a local café for a slow breakfast and people-watch. Explore any resort amenities you haven't used yet.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local art market or artisan village. Browse handmade silver jewelry, batik fabric, wood carvings, and paintings. This is a great opportunity to pick up budget-friendly souvenirs and gifts. Bargaining is expected and part of the fun.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a beach bar (order a single cocktail or stick to fresh juice to keep costs low). Watch the sky turn golden over the Indian Ocean. Enjoy a relaxed dinner at a new warung you haven't tried yet.

meals.breakfast: Slow café breakfast — avocado toast or banana pancakes with coffee. Budget: ~IDR 40,000–65,000 ($2.50–4 USD)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the art market area — fresh spring rolls or a bowl of soto ayam (chicken soup). Budget: ~IDR 35,000–60,000 ($2–4 USD)
meals.dinner: New warung discovery dinner — ask locals for their favorite spot. Try something you haven't eaten yet on the trip. Budget: ~IDR 50,000–80,000 ($3–5 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Today is intentionally relaxed. Use this day to do laundry (local laundry services cost ~IDR 15,000–25,000/kg), recharge devices, and plan your final days. Check if you need to book any remaining activities or transport.

day_by_day.morning: Join a full morning yoga class at a reputable local studio — look for a 90-minute class focusing on advanced flow or yin yoga. Many studios offer drop-in rates of IDR 100,000–150,000 ($6–10 USD). Take time to connect with other travelers and yogis.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Tirta Empul Temple — a sacred Hindu water temple where Balinese people perform purification rituals in holy spring water. Entry is ~IDR 50,000 ($3 USD). You can participate in the melukat (purification) ritual respectfully. Dress modestly and follow temple guidelines.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at a scenic cliff or viewpoint near the resort. If near Uluwatu, the cliff-top views are spectacular. Enjoy a final evening beach walk and buy some last-minute souvenirs from beach vendors.

meals.breakfast: Pre-yoga light meal — banana, granola bar, or a small smoothie. Budget: ~IDR 20,000–35,000 ($1–2 USD)
meals.lunch: Lunch near Tirta Empul — local warung with nasi campur (mixed rice plate). Budget: ~IDR 40,000–65,000 ($2.50–4 USD)
meals.dinner: Special budget treat dinner — find a slightly nicer warung or local restaurant for a celebratory meal. Try a full Balinese rijsttafel (rice table) spread. Budget: ~IDR 80,000–120,000 ($5–7 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Tirta Empul is one of Bali's most spiritually significant sites. Bring a change of clothes if you plan to enter the holy pools. Be respectful of worshippers and avoid visiting during active ceremonies unless invited. This is a deeply meaningful cultural experience.

day_by_day.morning: Final beach morning — wake up early for one last sunrise on the beach. Bring your yoga mat for a personal practice as the sun rises over the ocean. Take photos, breathe deeply, and soak in the beauty of Bali one last time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon doing any last-minute shopping, visiting spots you may have missed, or simply lounging on the beach. Pack non-essentials and begin organizing your luggage. Visit a local spa for a final Balinese massage as a farewell treat (IDR 80,000–120,000).
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at your favorite warung from the trip. Revisit a place that made an impression on you. Share a meal, leave a tip, and say goodbye to the staff who served you throughout your stay.

meals.breakfast: Sunrise beach breakfast — fresh fruit platter and coconut water from a beach vendor. Budget: ~IDR 30,000–50,000 ($2–3 USD)
meals.lunch: Light lunch — keep it simple as you're packing and preparing. Indomie noodles from a warung or a sandwich from a café. Budget: ~IDR 20,000–40,000 ($1.50–2.50 USD)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at your favorite spot from the trip. Splurge slightly if budget allows. Budget: ~IDR 80,000–120,000 ($5–7 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Begin packing tonight. Set aside any items for checked baggage vs. carry-on. Keep your travel documents, phone charger, and essentials accessible. Confirm your departure flight details and arrange your airport transfer for the following day.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Bali. Wake up and enjoy one last slow breakfast. Take a short final walk on the beach or sit quietly and reflect on your 13-day journey. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort — confirm checkout time with reception (usually 11 AM or 12 PM).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your flight time, store luggage at the hotel or head directly to Ngurah Rai International Airport. Arrive at the airport at least 2–3 hours before your international flight. Browse duty-free shops for last-minute Balinese coffee, chocolate, or snacks as gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Board your departure flight. Reflect on an incredible 13 days in Bali — beaches, yoga, culture, food, and unforgettable experiences — all on a budget!

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or a local café farewell meal — nasi goreng or your Bali favorite. Budget: ~IDR 30,000–50,000 ($2–3 USD)
meals.lunch: Airport food or a final warung meal before heading to the airport. Budget: ~IDR 50,000–80,000 ($3–5 USD)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal. Budget: ~IDR 60,000–100,000 ($4–6 USD) if purchasing at airport

day_by_day.notes: Allow extra time for airport check-in during July (peak travel season) — queues can be long. Keep a small amount of IDR for last-minute airport expenses. Exchange leftover rupiah before leaving or at the airport. Safe travels and until next time, Bali!

trip_options.title: Classic Bali Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Ngurah Rai International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear immigration, collect baggage, and arrange pre-booked airport transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort, Bali. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your beachfront accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable
meals.lunch: Not applicable
meals.dinner: Light snack or room service at the resort upon arrival — budget around IDR 80,000–150,000

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange airport transfer before travel to avoid late-night taxi hassles. Keep essentials like a change of clothes and toiletries in your carry-on for a comfortable first night. Exchange some currency at the airport or use an ATM for initial spending money.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take a slow stroll along the beachfront to orient yourself with the surroundings and watch the morning waves — a gentle introduction to Bali's coastal beauty.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the immediate beach area near the resort. Rent a sun lounger on the beach (IDR 50,000–100,000) and take your first dip in the warm Bali waters. Visit a nearby local warung or beach café to grab a fresh coconut and familiarise yourself with the neighbourhood.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed sunset from the beach — one of Bali's signature experiences. Head to a nearby beachside restaurant for a casual welcome dinner with fresh grilled seafood.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast buffet — included or IDR 120,000–200,000 if à la carte
meals.lunch: Local warung near the beach — nasi goreng or mie goreng — IDR 35,000–60,000
meals.dinner: Beachside seafood restaurant such as a local grilled fish spot — IDR 150,000–250,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Take it easy today — jet lag recovery is important. Apply sunscreen generously; even on cloudy days UV levels in Bali are high. The warm summer weather (avg 25°C) makes beach time very pleasant.

day_by_day.morning: Join a sunrise yoga session on the beach or at a nearby yoga studio. Many beachfront studios in Bali offer drop-in morning classes (IDR 100,000–180,000) starting around 07:00–08:00. Embrace the sound of the ocean as your backdrop for pranayama and asana practice.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local beach market or art market nearby to browse handmade crafts, sarongs, and souvenirs. Practice your bargaining skills! Spend time at the beach — try snorkelling if available near your resort area (equipment rental IDR 50,000–80,000).
day_by_day.evening: Explore a nearby village on foot or by scooter rental. Watch the sunset and enjoy a traditional Balinese dinner at a mid-range local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Smoothie bowl or avocado toast at a trendy health café near the beach — IDR 70,000–120,000
meals.lunch: Warung lunch — local Balinese babi guling (if not vegetarian) or gado-gado — IDR 40,000–70,000
meals.dinner: Traditional Balinese restaurant with rijsttafel-style set menu — IDR 180,000–280,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book yoga classes in advance if possible, especially during peak season in July. Bring a reusable water bottle — stay hydrated in the heat.

day_by_day.morning: Take a guided cultural morning tour to a nearby Hindu temple (such as a coastal sea temple). Dress respectfully — wear a sarong and sash (often provided at temple entrances). Witness morning offerings and learn about Balinese Hindu traditions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to a quieter, less-crowded beach cove nearby for an afternoon of swimming and relaxation. Bring a book, journal, or simply enjoy the calm turquoise waters. Alternatively, book a stand-up paddleboard (SUP) lesson — IDR 200,000–300,000 for 1–1.5 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Kecak fire dance performance at a nearby cultural venue if available in your area (IDR 100,000–150,000 per person). Follow with dinner at a mid-range restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Resort or guesthouse breakfast — fresh fruit, eggs, and Balinese coffee (kopi Bali)
meals.lunch: Beachside café — fresh salad, grilled fish sandwich, or nasi campur — IDR 80,000–130,000
meals.dinner: Mid-range Indonesian restaurant — IDR 150,000–220,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Check performance schedules in advance. Kecak performances typically begin at sunset (around 18:00–19:00). Carry a light layer for evenings as sea breezes can be cooling.

day_by_day.morning: Morning meditation and breathwork session — either self-guided on the beach at sunrise or through a guided class at a local wellness centre. Focus on grounding yourself midway through the trip. Spend time journaling or reading on the beach afterward.
day_by_day.afternoon: Day trip to a nearby waterfall or rice terrace viewpoint accessible from your coastal base (hire a driver for the day — IDR 400,000–600,000). Enjoy the lush green interior of Bali as a contrast to the coast. Take photos and enjoy the cooler inland microclimate.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Treat yourself to a traditional Balinese massage at a local spa — a one-hour massage costs IDR 150,000–250,000 at a reputable mid-range spa. End with a quiet dinner near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast — banana pancakes and fresh juice at a local café — IDR 60,000–100,000
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or eat at a warung near the waterfall/rice terrace — IDR 40,000–80,000
meals.dinner: Cosy restaurant near the resort — try sate lilit (Balinese minced fish satay) — IDR 130,000–200,000

day_by_day.notes: Negotiate the full-day driver rate in the morning and agree on all stops in advance. Waterfalls may have entrance fees of IDR 20,000–50,000. Wear comfortable walking shoes for inland excursions.

day_by_day.morning: Join a 90-minute sunrise yoga flow class at a beachfront yoga shala. Focus on a Vinyasa or Hatha class to energise for the day. Many studios offer themed classes on weekends — check local boards or Instagram for schedules.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore local surf culture — take a beginner or intermediate surf lesson on a nearby beach (IDR 250,000–400,000 including board and instructor for 2 hours). Bali's warm waters and consistent waves make it ideal for all levels.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a beach bonfire evening if available at your resort or a nearby beach club. Alternatively, visit a popular beach club for sundowners — enjoy one or two cocktails while watching the famous Bali sunset (budget IDR 100,000–200,000 for drinks).

meals.breakfast: Acai bowl, granola, or eggs at a health-focused café — IDR 80,000–130,000
meals.lunch: Post-surf meal at a beach shack — nasi goreng, fresh coconut, and fruit — IDR 50,000–90,000
meals.dinner: Beach club or mid-range restaurant dinner — grilled barramundi or prawn curry — IDR 200,000–300,000

day_by_day.notes: Apply waterproof sunscreen before surfing. Surf lessons are suitable for beginners — inform the instructor of your experience level. Rip currents can occur; always swim in designated areas.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and free morning. Sleep in, enjoy a slow breakfast, and spend time at the resort pool or beach. Use this mid-trip day to recharge, do laundry, and plan the second half of your trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local cooking class in the afternoon (IDR 350,000–500,000 per person, 3–4 hours). Learn to make traditional Balinese dishes such as lawar, tempeh manis, and black rice pudding. Classes often include a market visit.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the fruits of your cooking class labour — most classes end with eating what you cooked! Alternatively, stroll to a night market (pasar malam) for local street food and a vibrant local atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast — take your time and enjoy the spread
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort or a nearby café — IDR 80,000–120,000
meals.dinner: Dinner from cooking class OR night market street food — IDR 50,000–100,000 at the market

day_by_day.notes: Day 7 is intentionally lighter — a balanced trip needs rest days to avoid burnout. Use afternoon cooking class as a fun, interactive cultural activity rather than sightseeing. Book cooking class in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning beach walk to collect shells and watch fishing boats return with their catch. Visit a local fish market if one is nearby — a fascinating cultural experience. Return for a healthy breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a different beach section — rent a bicycle (IDR 50,000–80,000/day) and cycle along coastal paths to discover hidden coves and local temples along the shoreline. Stop for fresh coconuts along the way.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset photography session on the beach — the warm July light creates golden hour magic. Dine at a rooftop restaurant with ocean views for a special mid-trip treat.

meals.breakfast: Local warung breakfast — bubur ayam (rice porridge) or fried rice with egg — IDR 30,000–60,000
meals.lunch: Beachside café during cycling break — fresh fruit plate and iced tea — IDR 60,000–100,000
meals.dinner: Rooftop restaurant with ocean view — slightly splurge-worthy dinner — IDR 250,000–380,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Cycling is a wonderful low-impact way to explore coastal Bali. Wear a helmet if provided. Stay hydrated — carry water on your cycle tour. Check bike condition before renting.

day_by_day.morning: Attend a morning Yin Yoga or restorative yoga class — a slower-paced practice perfect for mid-trip muscle recovery. Focus on deep stretching and mindfulness. Many studios offer this style specifically in morning sessions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby sacred spring or holy water temple (Pura Tirta) for a purification ceremony experience. Dress modestly and follow local customs. Hire a local guide (IDR 100,000–150,000) to explain the spiritual significance.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a traditional Balinese dinner with a cultural show — some restaurants combine a set dinner with live gamelan music or Legong dance performance. A memorable evening experience (IDR 200,000–350,000 inclusive).

meals.breakfast: Smoothie, overnight oats, or fresh papaya at a wellness café — IDR 70,000–110,000
meals.lunch: Vegetarian warung near the temple — tofu satay, tempeh, steamed rice — IDR 40,000–70,000
meals.dinner: Cultural dinner show restaurant — IDR 200,000–350,000 per person inclusive of performance

day_by_day.notes: Bring a sarong and respectful clothing for temple visits. Some holy spring temples require a ritual purification process — follow all instructions given by the priest or guide. Photography rules vary — always ask before shooting.

day_by_day.morning: Water activity morning — try stand-up paddleboarding, kayaking, or a snorkelling trip to a nearby reef. Book through your resort or a local operator (IDR 200,000–400,000 depending on activity). The calm morning sea is ideal for water sports.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax on the beach and read or journal. Treat yourself to a beachside coconut oil massage or reflexology session from a local beach masseuse (IDR 100,000–150,000 for 60 minutes). Enjoy the warm afternoon sun.
day_by_day.evening: Explore a nearby town's restaurant strip for dinner. Try a different cuisine — Bali has excellent Italian, Japanese, and Mexican restaurants alongside Indonesian options, reflecting its cosmopolitan expat community.

meals.breakfast: Resort or hotel breakfast — fuel up before water activities
meals.lunch: Fresh juice bar and light snacks after water sports — IDR 60,000–100,000
meals.dinner: International restaurant for variety — wood-fired pizza or Japanese ramen — IDR 150,000–250,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Confirm water activity bookings the evening before. Bring reef-safe sunscreen for snorkelling to protect coral ecosystems. Avoid touching or standing on coral reefs.

day_by_day.morning: Final yoga deep-dive — attend a 2-hour yoga workshop or masterclass at a renowned local studio. Topics might include arm balances, pranayama techniques, or meditation deepening. A rewarding investment in your practice (IDR 200,000–350,000).
day_by_day.afternoon: Shopping afternoon — visit local boutiques, art galleries, and handicraft shops for final souvenirs. Look for hand-carved wooden items, silver jewellery, batik fabric, and Balinese paintings. Support local artisans where possible.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell pre-dinner sunset cocktail on the beach. Reflect on the journey and enjoy Bali's famous golden hour one final time. Dine at your favourite restaurant from the trip for a nostalgic last full evening.

meals.breakfast: Healthy café breakfast — acai bowl, chia pudding, or eggs Benedict — IDR 90,000–150,000
meals.lunch: Light warung lunch while shopping — nasi campur or gado-gado — IDR 40,000–70,000
meals.dinner: Return to your favourite restaurant from the trip — budget IDR 200,000–300,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Bargaining is expected at markets but be respectful and fair. Keep receipts for any larger purchases. Ensure souvenirs comply with customs regulations in your home country (no live plants, certain animal products, etc.).

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise beach meditation — sit quietly on the sand, watch the sun rise over the ocean, and practice gratitude for the journey. A peaceful, personal ritual to close the Bali chapter. Take a final morning swim in the warm Indian Ocean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check-out procedures and luggage storage at the resort. Spend the afternoon at the resort pool or beach if check-out is early. Do a final walk through the local area — revisit a favourite spot, café, or viewpoint.
day_by_day.evening: Depending on departure flight timing — either a relaxed farewell dinner at the resort or a light meal near the airport. Begin preparing for departure: repack, check documents, confirm transport to airport.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — enjoy the last morning spread fully
meals.lunch: Favourite local warung for a nostalgic last Balinese meal — IDR 50,000–100,000
meals.dinner: Light dinner at resort or airport-area restaurant — IDR 100,000–180,000

day_by_day.notes: Confirm airport transfer booking. Ngurah Rai Airport is busy — arrive at least 2.5–3 hours before international flights. Keep carry-on essentials accessible. Check for any last-minute Bali departure tax requirements.

day_by_day.morning: Departure day. If time permits, enjoy a final breakfast at the resort or a nearby café. Complete any last-minute packing and ensure all personal items are collected from the room safe and bathroom.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Ngurah Rai International Airport. Allow extra time for traffic — Bali roads can be congested, especially near Kuta and Denpasar. Complete check-in, immigration, and security procedures.
day_by_day.evening: Board your departure flight. Carry a Balinese snack (like kacang bali or rempeyek) for the journey home. Reflect on 13 days of beaches, yoga, culture, and balance — and begin planning your return to the Island of the Gods.

meals.breakfast: Final Balinese breakfast — fresh tropical fruit, Balinese coffee, and rice cake — IDR 60,000–100,000
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant or lounge — IDR 100,000–200,000
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport dining depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Keep all boarding passes, passport, and travel insurance documents easily accessible. Declare any food items at customs upon return home. Consider downloading offline maps and translation apps before losing local SIM data. Selamat jalan — safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Bali Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled – late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled – late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Ngurah Rai International Airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged by Aegean Bliss Resort awaits you at arrivals. Check in to your Beachfront suite, enjoy a welcome drink and a light late-night amenity platter prepared by the resort. Unwind on your private terrace listening to the ocean.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable – in-flight or pre-arrival
meals.lunch: Not applicable – in-flight or pre-arrival
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome amenity platter and champagne provided by Aegean Bliss Resort upon check-in

day_by_day.notes: Ensure private airport transfer is pre-booked through the resort concierge. Keep Day 1 light – rest is the priority after a long flight. Luggage will be unpacked by butler service if requested.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and ease into Bali time. Begin the morning with a private sunrise yoga session on your beachfront terrace or the resort's dedicated open-air yoga pavilion overlooking the Indian Ocean. A certified instructor from the resort guides you through a gentle Hatha flow to reset the body after travel.
day_by_day.afternoon: After a leisurely brunch, take a guided orientation walk along the resort's private beach stretch. Spend the afternoon at the resort's infinity pool with butler service, sipping fresh coconut water and tropical juices. Optional: a 90-minute Balinese welcome massage at the resort spa to ease jet lag.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's beachfront bar. Dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant featuring contemporary Indonesian cuisine with fresh local seafood.

meals.breakfast: Lavish à la carte breakfast at the resort's ocean-view restaurant – try the Nasi Goreng royale with free-range eggs and fresh tropical fruit platters
meals.lunch: Poolside gourmet lunch at the resort's cabana dining service – grilled barramundi, prawn skewers, and fresh açaí bowls
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort signature restaurant – tasting menu featuring Balinese spiced lobster, duck confit rendang, and pandan panna cotta

day_by_day.notes: Keep this day relaxed and resort-focused to recover from travel. Book the spa massage in advance through the concierge. Sunset cocktail hour typically begins at 18:00.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning 90-minute Vinyasa yoga class at the resort's clifftop yoga shala with panoramic ocean views. Following yoga, join a guided snorkeling excursion departing from the resort's private beach – explore vibrant coral gardens and tropical fish in the warm, clear waters off the Bali coast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private speedboat charter to a secluded nearby sandbar or nearby pristine cove for a private beach picnic lunch. Swim, sunbathe, and enjoy the exclusivity of a hidden Balinese beach accessible only by boat. Return to the resort by mid-afternoon for free time.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a nearby premium beachside lounge for sundowners. Dinner at a renowned local luxury restaurant in the Seminyak or Jimbaran area known for fresh grilled seafood served on the beach under lanterns.

meals.breakfast: Pre-yoga light smoothie bowl and cold-pressed juices at the resort wellness café
meals.lunch: Private gourmet beach picnic on the sandbar – curated by the resort chef with chilled prawns, artisan cheeses, tropical fruits, and sparkling wine
meals.dinner: Jimbaran Bay-style premium beachfront seafood dinner – whole grilled lobster, tiger prawns, and snapper with sambal and lime, served at the water's edge

day_by_day.notes: Confirm speedboat charter and private picnic at least 24 hours in advance with the resort concierge. Bring reef-safe sunscreen for snorkeling. July weather is ideal – expect calm seas and excellent visibility.

day_by_day.morning: Morning Yin Yoga and meditation session at the resort's beachfront pavilion focused on deep stretching and mindfulness. Afterward, take a private cooking class hosted by the resort's executive chef – learn to prepare traditional Balinese dishes including satay lilit, black rice pudding, and lawar.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local area with a private guided cultural tour – visit a nearby traditional Balinese village, a sea temple (Pura Tanah Lot is within reach), and local artisan markets. Your private driver and guide will handle all logistics.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a private in-villa dining experience on your beachfront terrace. The resort butler sets up a romantic candlelit table with a curated 5-course menu and wine pairing as the waves lap the shore.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast buffet with live cooking stations – eggs benedict, fresh juices, Balinese jamu wellness shots
meals.lunch: Dishes prepared during your own cooking class enjoyed together in the resort's garden dining area
meals.dinner: Private in-villa 5-course dinner on your beachfront terrace – curated by the resort chef with Balinese-French fusion menu and sommelier-selected wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly with a sarong when visiting temples – the resort can provide these. Tanah Lot is best visited in the afternoon when the tide recedes. Book in-villa dining 24 hours ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise stand-up paddleboard (SUP) session along the calm morning ocean with an instructor from the resort. Follow with a 60-minute restorative yoga and breathwork session on the beach. Enjoy a slow, indulgent breakfast with ocean views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Full afternoon at the resort's luxury spa – begin with a traditional Balinese boreh body scrub using rice, ginger, and clove, followed by a 2-hour Royal Balinese massage and a floral bath ritual. Complete the experience in the spa's relaxation lounge with herbal teas.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private traditional Balinese Kecak fire dance performance arranged by the resort – a mesmerizing cultural spectacle performed at sunset. Dinner at a world-class restaurant in the Seminyak area renowned for its creative Asian fusion tasting menu.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely à la carte breakfast at the resort – avocado toast with Balinese spices, smoked salmon, fresh tropical juices and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Light spa lunch at the wellness café – cold-pressed juices, grain bowls, and raw desserts to complement the spa day
meals.dinner: Premium Asian fusion restaurant in Seminyak – wagyu beef tataki, Balinese duck confit, and yuzu miso black cod with sake pairing

day_by_day.notes: Book the full spa day package in advance – it is one of the resort's most popular offerings. The Kecak fire dance can also be experienced at Uluwatu Temple for an even more dramatic clifftop setting – confirm with concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided surf lesson on a nearby beginner-friendly beach with a professional ISA-certified instructor. The warm July waters and consistent swells make this an ideal time to try surfing or refine your technique. Followed by a post-surf stretch and yoga cool-down on the beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the artistic hub of Seminyak or nearby Canggu by private car – browse high-end Balinese boutiques, local art galleries, and design stores. Visit a renowned concept store for premium Balinese crafts and fashion. Optional: a curated art gallery visit featuring contemporary Balinese artists.
day_by_day.evening: Rooftop cocktails at one of Bali's most exclusive sky bars with 360-degree sunset views. Dinner at a celebrated chef's table restaurant in Seminyak – an intimate 8-seat experience with a live chef-narrated tasting menu.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort – fresh fruit, granola, yogurt, and cold brew coffee before the surf lesson
meals.lunch: Trendy café lunch in Seminyak or Canggu – superfood bowls, artisan sandwiches, and specialty single-origin coffee at a premium lifestyle café
meals.dinner: Chef's table tasting experience – 8-course progressive Indonesian fine dining with local wine and artisanal spirit pairings

day_by_day.notes: Surfing is best in the morning when winds are offshore. Bring a change of clothes for the afternoon shopping excursion. Chef's table reservations must be made well in advance – the resort concierge can assist.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to Ubud – depart early by private luxury vehicle. Begin with a guided walk through the iconic Tegalalang Rice Terraces at their most photogenic in the morning light. Follow with a visit to a sacred monkey forest sanctuary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore central Ubud – visit the Royal Palace (Puri Saren Agung), browse the Ubud Art Market for premium handicrafts, and tour a renowned local artist's studio or gallery. Afternoon visit to a traditional healer (Balian) or a premium Ubud wellness retreat for a short meditation session.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset dinner in Ubud at a jungle-edge luxury restaurant with dramatic views over the Ayung River gorge and rice terraces. Return to the resort by private car after dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast – packed or quick service before departure to Ubud
meals.lunch: Premium farm-to-table lunch at a celebrated Ubud organic restaurant set among the rice paddies – local vegetables, tempeh, and Balinese slow-cooked meats
meals.dinner: Clifftop jungle restaurant in Ubud – Balinese suckling pig (babi guling), river fish in banana leaf, and exotic tropical desserts with panoramic gorge views

day_by_day.notes: Ubud is approximately 1–1.5 hours from the coastal resort area. Depart by 07:30 to make the most of the day. Dress respectfully for temple and palace visits. Bring a light layer for the Ubud highlands which can be slightly cooler.

day_by_day.morning: Recovery and wellness morning – begin with a 75-minute Pranayama breathwork and meditation class at the resort's beachfront shala. Follow with a guided sound healing bowl therapy session in the resort's garden sanctuary. Enjoy a slow, nourishing breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private catamaran sailing charter – spend the afternoon sailing along the Bali coastline, anchoring at pristine snorkeling spots and hidden coves. Enjoy the warm July sunshine, crystal waters, and onboard catering with chilled champagne and gourmet snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowners on the catamaran as you sail back to shore during golden hour. Evening at leisure – optional visit to a luxury beach club for dinner and live acoustic music.

meals.breakfast: Wellness breakfast at the resort – detox juices, raw granola, chia pudding, poached eggs, and herbal teas
meals.lunch: Onboard catamaran gourmet catering – chilled seafood platter, artisan bread, tropical fruits, and premium sparkling wine
meals.dinner: Premium Bali beach club dinner – wood-fired pizzas, fresh sashimi, and grilled meats with a DJ or live acoustic set in a sophisticated open-air setting

day_by_day.notes: Catamaran charters typically run 4–6 hours. Book through the resort concierge at least 2 days in advance. Apply reef-safe sunscreen throughout the day. July is peak sailing season with ideal wind and sea conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning private yoga session on the beach at sunrise followed by a guided coastal hike or nature walk along scenic clifftop paths near the resort area. Explore dramatic ocean vistas, blowholes, and lush coastal vegetation with a knowledgeable local guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Indulge in a long, leisurely afternoon at the resort. Rent a private cabana at the pool, enjoy butler-served refreshments, and read or simply relax. Optional: a 60-minute reflexology or foot massage at the spa.
day_by_day.evening: Private beachside bonfire dinner arranged by the resort – a romantic setup with tiki torches, a fire pit, and a personalized 4-course menu served under the stars directly on the beach.

meals.breakfast: Post-hike resort breakfast – protein-rich options including smoked salmon bagels, egg white omelets, fresh fruit, and cold-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Poolside light lunch – mezze-style sharing plates, fresh salads, grilled chicken skewers, and tropical smoothies
meals.dinner: Private beachside bonfire dinner – lobster bisque, grilled whole fish, Balinese spiced lamb chops, and coconut pandan crème brûlée with fine wine

day_by_day.notes: The beachside bonfire dinner is a signature experience at Aegean Bliss Resort – book at least 48 hours in advance. Bring a light wrap for the evening as the sea breeze can be refreshing after sunset.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Uluwatu Peninsula – depart by private car to explore the dramatic clifftop Uluwatu Temple perched 70 meters above the Indian Ocean. Enjoy guided commentary on the temple's history and Hindu significance. Walk the clifftop paths with stunning panoramic ocean views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to the world-renowned Uluwatu surf beaches – Padang Padang or Bingin Beach. Enjoy a beach club lunch with front-row views of expert surfers. Explore the cave beach access points and limestone cliff formations unique to the Bukit Peninsula.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the legendary Kecak fire dance at Uluwatu Temple at sunset – one of Bali's most spectacular cultural performances set against the ocean backdrop. Dinner at a premium clifftop restaurant in Uluwatu with sweeping ocean views.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure – continental spread with fresh pastries, tropical fruits, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Premium Uluwatu beach club lunch – fresh tuna tartare, grilled seafood, açaí bowls, and craft cocktails with a view of the surf
meals.dinner: Clifftop fine-dining restaurant in Uluwatu – premium wagyu beef, Balinese-spiced seafood risotto, and exotic desserts with an uninterrupted Indian Ocean panorama

day_by_day.notes: Wear a sarong at Uluwatu Temple – these are provided at the entrance. Beware of the temple monkeys who may snatch sunglasses or loose items. The Kecak dance begins at approximately 18:00 – arrive 30 minutes early for the best seats.

day_by_day.morning: Morning Ashtanga yoga master class with a senior instructor at the resort – a more dynamic and challenging practice for those looking to deepen their yoga journey. Follow with a guided meditation and journaling session in the resort's garden sanctuary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon wellness immersion at the resort spa – enjoy a 3-hour luxury spa journey including a Javanese lulur body treatment, herbal steam room, cold plunge pool, and a signature Balinese facial. Completely surrender to relaxation.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-style premium dinner at the resort's most exclusive dining venue – request the chef's special off-menu experience or the resort's signature 7-course degustation. Enjoy live traditional Balinese gamelan music during dinner.

meals.breakfast: Nourishing pre-yoga breakfast – overnight oats, banana and almond butter, fresh juices, and green tea
meals.lunch: Post-spa wellness lunch at the resort's health-focused café – detox broths, grain bowls, and raw desserts
meals.dinner: Resort's premium degustation dinner – 7-course Balinese-French fusion menu with champagne and wine pairings, accompanied by live gamelan music

day_by_day.notes: The Ashtanga class is physically demanding – inform the instructor of any injuries or limitations. The spa journey package should be booked 48 hours in advance. Gamelan music performances are typically available on select evenings – confirm with concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Final full morning – slow sunrise yoga and meditation on your private beachfront terrace. Take a long, peaceful walk along the resort's private beach, collecting memories and taking in the beauty of Bali's coastline one last time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last indulgent afternoon at the resort – spend time at the infinity pool, enjoy a final spa treatment (choose a 60-minute express option), and take time to shop for premium Balinese souvenirs and gifts at the resort boutique or a nearby luxury shop.
day_by_day.evening: Special farewell dinner at a celebrated premium restaurant – choose a rooftop venue or a beachfront establishment for a memorable final night in Bali. Celebrate the journey with a bottle of fine wine or champagne.

meals.breakfast: Grand final breakfast at the resort – order everything you loved throughout the trip; indulge in a full spread of Balinese and international favorites
meals.lunch: Light and fresh poolside lunch – cold seafood salad, tropical fruit sorbet, and sparkling water or light rosé
meals.dinner: Celebratory farewell dinner at a premium Bali restaurant – whole roasted lobster, premium wagyu, and a decadent dessert platter with a bottle of vintage champagne

day_by_day.notes: Begin packing and organizing luggage this evening. Confirm departure transfer with the resort concierge. Purchase any last-minute gifts or premium Balinese products – vanilla pods, artisan coffee, and premium spa products make excellent souvenirs.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Bali – wake up for one last sunrise on the beach. Enjoy a peaceful final breakfast at the resort. Complete check-out formalities assisted by the resort butler who handles all luggage and documentation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time, enjoy a final swim or simply relax in the resort's day-use facilities. The resort can arrange a late check-out or day-use room if your flight departs in the evening. Private luxury transfer to Ngurah Rai International Airport arranged by the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Bali with extraordinary memories of 13 days of luxury, yoga, beaches, and Balinese culture. Airport lounge access recommended – the resort concierge can arrange premium lounge passes.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast – a personal favorite selection enjoyed slowly with ocean views as a perfect send-off
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at the resort or airport lounge depending on departure time – fresh sandwiches, salads, and tropical juices
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight premium meal – request a special meal option when booking your return flight

day_by_day.notes: Confirm airport transfer timing based on your departure flight. Allow at least 3 hours before departure for international check-in and immigration. Keep all receipts for any VAT refund claims at the airport. Bali's airport has a premium duty-free area for last-minute luxury purchases.
